Well I finally finished! Took about 5 months. After reading most of TCG I could not figure out how it was going to resolve in just 50 final pages.

I'm only kinda satisfied by the ending...only because I'm left with so many questions.

First, the overall series is fantastic. It was a great epic series with endearing characters and complexities. I'm not sure I will restart anytime soon but I am interested in going back through GotM to see what I missed the first time around.

My questions at the end:

What happened to Grub? Didn't Envy and Spite survive - why didn't they find their father? Fiddler gets home but where did Tavore and Paran go? Does Tavore know she killed Fellisan? What "foreign world" is the Crippled God from? Is it accessible to the Malazan world via warren or totally separate? What happened to Kallor? How exactly was Ruuthan Gudd associated with Kallor? I'll admit I'm confused by the way Cotillion kills the Crippled God...was that a release for him from that world or true death?

Even though the main series is over it seems to me there are many loose ends that can be tied up with future novels. Karsa, the gods, Hood, Shadownthrone, Iskaral Pust, Dharujistan...so much life still in that world.
Finished main series (Spoilers - All: main series)

First of all, congratulations on finishing the series.

As to your questions I think Erikson is very deliberate in leaving so many threads open. Just like the series doesn't have a proper beginning, i.e. the reader is just dropped into the middle of the world where you have to figure things out on your own. I think it's only appropriate that the end of the series doesn't provide closure for everyone. It is rather implied that they are not yet done.

But you can rejoice in that Erikson is planning a Karsa trilogy after he's done with the Kharkanas trilogy. Then we also have Esslemont who, as far as I know, isn't planning on stopping writing any time soon.

Thanks! Good point about the beginning and the end. Would be interesting to see an outline of their envisioned future stories. They have such an awesome world - there is much opportunity.

In the Karsa series I hope he goes into more around his first meeting with his daughters. That seemed totally glossed over in the main series.
